answer: Reputation is a scarce, unforgeable resource earned by consistently passing originality checks, and the economy spends it to filter out Sybil clusters before they can compound into a majority. The design works because cost compounds over compute, time, and reputation, growing faster than the influence the cluster can extract. The effect is that voting power tracks real contribution, so a flood of accounts cannot outvote a smaller set of genuinely established participants. Consider a beacon as the anchor of the cost.
